item.title: Genesis and Evolution of Panchayati Raj in Sikkim: From Traditional Governance to Constitutional Democracy
item.description:
Genesis and Evolution of Panchayati Raj in Sikkim

The Panchayati Raj system in Sikkim has evolved through several stages over nearly eight decades. Beginning as a traditional village-level administrative arrangement during the erstwhile Kingdom of Sikkim, it gradually transformed into a constitutionally recognized system of democratic local self-government after Sikkim became a state of India.

Today, Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) form the foundation of rural governance in Sikkim. They play a vital role in local planning, implementation of development programmes, delivery of public services, and promoting participatory democracy.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Local Body Audits: Comprehensive Requisition Checklists, Financial Formats, and Compliance Frameworks for GPUs, ZPs, and Municipalities
item.description:
Conducting a statutory or internal audit of local self-government institutions—such as Gram Panchayat Units (GPUs), Zilla Panchayats (ZPs), and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) or Municipalities—requires a structured, systematic approach. Auditing these bodies involves verifying not only cash transactions and bank balances but also statutory compliance, public procurement guidelines, revenue realisations, and asset registers.

This comprehensive guide compiles every essential checklist, fillable requisition format, financial reporting template, and technical explanation needed to prepare for or execute an audit of local governing bodies.

item.title: Understanding the 16th Finance Commission Grants for Rural Local Bodies: A Comprehensive Overview and State Action Plan
item.description:

item.title: Decoding Local Governance & Audit Insights: A Comprehensive Review of CAG Reports on Sikkim's PRIs and ULBs
item.description:
Decoding Local Governance & Audit Insights: A Comprehensive Review of CAG Reports on Sikkim’s PRIs and ULBs

Local self-governance forms the bedrock of grassroots democracy in India. Envisaged under the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) are mandated to drive economic development, social justice, and local public service delivery. However, the operational reality on the ground often reveals systemic gaps between policy intent and execution.
